title: Ser, consistir en y oraciones de relativo: definir la nación

sections.content: Ser states what something is (or isn't); consistir en spells out what it's made of; a relative clause with que folds a definition into the same sentence instead of starting a new one. Together they're the toolkit for precise definition. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Una nación no es simplemente un territorio con fronteras dibujadas en un mapa.
items.english: A nation is not simply a territory with borders drawn on a map.

items.spanish: Una nación consiste en un grupo de personas que comparten, o creen compartir, una historia y un destino común.
items.english: A nation consists of a group of people who share, or believe they share, a history and a common destiny.

items.spanish: Una nación es una comunidad imaginada porque la inmensa mayoría de sus miembros nunca se conocerán entre sí.
items.english: A nation is an imagined community because the vast majority of its members will never meet each other.

items.spanish: Esa construcción, que consistía en crear símbolos, relatos y rituales compartidos, no era un proceso natural.
items.english: That construction, which consisted of creating shared symbols, stories and rituals, was not a natural process.

sections.content: Consistir en always takes en before its complement (consiste EN un grupo, consistía EN crear) — a common error is dropping the en, but the verb needs it to introduce what something is made up of.
